source.title: On skip connections and normalisation layers in deep optimisation
source.authors: L. MacDonald; Jack Valmadre; Hemanth Saratchandran; Simon Lucey

record.tranche_reason: The study experimentally tests whether skip-connection changes improve training speed, using singular-value analysis and training-loss comparisons. It does not test the training-error, depth-scaling, or normalization conditions named in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own skip-connection experiments. The theoretical convergence theorem and statements about prior work are not empirical result rows. The reported training-loss curves are figure-only; no curve values are reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether deterministic skip components improve Jacobian singular values and training speed. None of V1–V6 names that comparison: it does not measure training classification error, vary depth or initialization, compare normalization recipes, or locate learning-rate stability thresholds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors also present a framework for loss smoothness and regularity and claim a global-convergence proof covering optima at infinity for a restricted network class. Their practical experiments support modest training-speed improvements from deterministic skip additions, without directly testing that theorem.
record.recipe_differences: Uses default PyTorch initialization and empirical skip-connection modifications to compare training speed; the recipes and measures differ from those in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The CIFAR and ImageNet experiments varied learning rates; the modified ImageNet architecture did not converge at learning rate 0.2. The paper reports CIFAR validation accuracies were not statistically significantly different, while ImageNet validation accuracy was statistically significantly better for the modified model.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding deterministic skip components increases mean composite-Jacobian singular values from 2.36 to 2.91 to 3.17 across Chain, Res and ResAvg, with faster convergence reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deterministic skip components can increase layer-Jacobian singular values and accelerate initial training at fixed depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding average-pool components to convolutional skips modestly improves training speed in the selected CIFAR and ImageNet settings. The modified ImageNet model fails to converge at learning rate 0.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding deterministic components to projection skips can modestly accelerate ResNet training, with benefits dependent on learning rate and setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5.1 gives a global-convergence guarantee for specially normalized residual networks under restrictive data and architecture assumptions, which the authors say typical practical networks do not satisfy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A restricted class of normalized residual networks admits global-convergence guarantees from any initialization at a sufficiently small learning rate.

record.problems: The practical experiments measure training loss and speed rather than training classification error. The CIFAR and ImageNet loss curves are figure-only; the CIFAR10 learning-rate 0.2 original model diverged in 6 out of 10 trials, and the ImageNet modification did not converge at learning rate 0.2. The theorem's assumptions are stated not to hold for typical deep-learning problems.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure 6's additional ImageNet loss plots at learning rates 0.2, 0.05 and 0.02 are not separately extracted because the paper gives the curve values only as plots and reports the learning-rate 0.2 non-convergence in the limitation excerpt; the figure caption and Table 3 also report this condition.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping time and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training degradation as depth increases, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and initialization-dependent trainable depth.
Recovery above an initial stability threshold, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Batch normalization versus unnormalized training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats final training losses as unavailable numerically; Tables 1–3 report them. Low cross-entropy alone does not supply the training classification error required by V1. Learning-rate failures without measured stability thresholds do not test V5. No verdict is warranted for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model size or training-duration effects.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth-dependent training error and comparisons of plain versus residual networks at increasing depth; identity shortcuts as specified in the claim.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for signal propagation, learning speed, or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises, curvature or sharpness behavior, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup or other normalization-free training recipes.

rows.subject: Chain
rows.operation_detail: Measured composite-layer Jacobian singular values over the first 10 training iterations and training loss on 32 randomly chosen MNIST training points.
rows.measure: Composite-layer Jacobian singular-value distribution and training loss curve.
rows.value: Figure 2 reports a mean singular value of 2.36; training-loss value is figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Means over 10 trials shown; no uncertainty stated for the singular-value mean.
rows.note: The loss curve is not numerically reported. This is the chain comparison model.
rows.check: The Chain network is batch-normalized; add this condition. Its Jacobian singular values and loss curve do not establish any listed version.

rows.subject: Res
rows.operation_detail: Grouped convolutional layers 2–3 and 5–6 into two residual blocks, including a 1x1 convolutional skip in the second block; measured composite-layer Jacobian singular values and training loss.
rows.measure: Composite-layer Jacobian singular-value distribution and training loss curve.
rows.baseline: Chain comparison; loss value not stated.
rows.value: Figure 2 reports a mean singular value of 2.91; training-loss value is figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Means over 10 trials shown; no uncertainty stated for the singular-value mean.
rows.note: The authors state the distributions shift upward as deterministic skips are added, resulting in faster convergence.
rows.check: This fixed-depth comparison measures the effect of adding residual blocks, without testing depth-dependent degradation. All three MNIST models use batch normalization.

rows.subject: ResAvg
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the 1x1 convolutional skip with an average-pool skip rescaled to have all singular values equal to 1, added to the convolutional skip; measured composite-layer Jacobian singular values and training loss.
rows.measure: Composite-layer Jacobian singular-value distribution and training loss curve.
rows.baseline: Chain and Res comparisons; loss values not stated.
rows.value: Figure 2 reports a mean singular value of 3.17; training-loss value is figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Means over 10 trials shown; no uncertainty stated for the singular-value mean.
rows.note: The authors state the distributions shift upward as deterministic skips are added, resulting in faster convergence.
rows.check: Correct the operation: retain the convolutional skip A and add a rescaled average-pool component I, producing I+A. The average pool alone does not replace A. All three MNIST models use batch normalization.

rows.subject: PreAct-ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss for the original architecture.
rows.note: The paper says the modified architecture improves training speed; the plotted values are not given numerically.
rows.check: The curve is figure-only, but Table 1 supplies final training loss at learning rate 0.1: 0.0032 ± 0.0002. This is loss, not training classification error.

rows.subject: PreAct-ResNet18

rows.note: The paper states the modification improves training speed.
rows.check: Table 1 supplies final training loss at learning rate 0.1: 0.0022 ± 0.0002, versus original 0.0032 ± 0.0002. This architecture comparison does not measure a listed version.
